g.text: NWIS Drilling Engineer Decision Support Workflow
A systematic 7-stage pipeline transforming raw historical offset-well records into real-time, depth-aware drilling hazard advisories.
Drilling engineer selects target wellbore coordinates and spud metadata.
Read active depth (3,842m MD) via demo telemetry or manual depth slider.
Executes geodesic distance filter against historical wellbore coordinate repository.
Engineer dynamically adjusts search buffer between 1 km and 20 km.
Filters hundreds of regional basin boreholes down to actionable offset cluster.
Ranks high-impact offsets above distant or structurally disparate boreholes.
Inspectable weighted sum prevents black-box confusion for drilling teams.
Normalizes Measured Depth (MD) to True Vertical Depth (TVD) across wells.
Correlates formation tops (F1, F2, F3) across regional structural strike & dip.
Compares rate of penetration (ROP), torque, and mud weight trends.
Scans 50m to 200m ahead of active bit into uncharted immediate depth.
Identifies kicks, severe losses, tight holes, and stuck pipe occurrences in offset wells.
Categorizes historical events into Low, Medium, High, and Critical alert tiers.
Extracts exact historical text, operator shift notes, and rig remarks.
Surfaces mechanical or geologic origins (e.g. natural fracture network vs surge pressure).
Retrieves successful remedies applied by previous drilling teams.
Presents high-visibility warning to rig crew before penetrating loss zone.
Answers ad-hoc engineer queries with direct clickable citations to DDR records.
Generates shift-handover intelligence brief for morning operational alignment.

NWIS functions strictly as a decision-support advisory system. It never commands rig actuators or replaces mud engineers. The drilling superintendent and company representative review all historical insights before adjusting mud weight or rotary speeds.

Every risk alert and Copilot recommendation maps directly to an authenticated source file, paragraph number, and recorded borehole log. Rig crews can cross-verify findings instantly against physical Oil India completion reports without speculation.

Instead of reacting after a kick or severe circulation loss occurs, NWIS projects ahead of the bit (50–200m). This grants crews 4 to 8 hours of advance operational buffer to condition mud systems, pre-stage lost circulation material, and inspect BHA.
SIH 2026 • PROBLEM PS26121 • CONCEPTUAL WORKFLOW VISUAL
